title: JSONata
subtitle: Query and reshape JSON with compact expressions
intro: Filter nested arrays, construct output objects, and aggregate values within a JSON document. JSONata keeps these transformations in one SQL expression and returns JSON that can be cast, extracted, or expanded by DuckDB.

reference.name: jsonata(expr, data)
reference.description: Evaluate an expression against a JSON document.

reference.name: jsonata(expr, data, bindings)
reference.description: Bind JSON object keys as $variables in the expression.

reference.name: Account.Name
reference.description: Follow nested fields using dotted paths.

reference.name: items[price > $limit]
reference.description: Filter array members by a predicate.

reference.name: {"total": $sum(prices)}
reference.description: Construct an output object with an aggregate.

reference.name: [expression]
reference.description: Use array construction when a stable array shape matters.

notes.title: Bind values, keep expressions stable
notes.body: Pass thresholds and other parameters through the bindings object instead of concatenating them into the expression. Its keys omit the dollar sign: {"limit": 100} is read as $limit inside JSONata.

notes.title: Pay attention to result shape
notes.body: JSONata sequences can collapse to a single value. Wrap a projection in array construction when downstream SQL expects JSON[]. The function returns JSON; cast numbers explicitly or use DuckDB JSON extractors for strings.

examples.title: Filter with a bound threshold
examples.caption: The outer brackets preserve an array for one matching item.

examples.title: Build a summary object
examples.caption: Construct several output fields without unpacking the document.

examples.title: Return a SQL number
examples.caption: Cast the JSON result before joining or doing typed SQL arithmetic.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN jsonata('[items[price > $limit].id]', '{"items":[{"id":"A","price":20},{"id":"B","price":120}]}', '{"limit":100}')::VARCHAR = '["B"]' AND jsonata('$sum(prices)', '{"prices":[12,18,5]}')::INTEGER = 35 THEN true ELSE error('JSONata result mismatch') END;
